message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| 2 | **Gather Parts** | All components must fit together. | Use a PC build checklist or a site like PCPartPicker to avoid incompatibilities. |
| 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Anti‑static wrist strap or mat; work on a non‑conductive surface. |
| 4 | **Open the Case** | Access the interior. | Remove side panels, unscrew screws, set aside. |
| 5 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components. | Place PSU with the fan facing down or toward the rear exhaust. Secure with screws. |
| 6 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for all other parts. | Align standoffs with motherboard holes, screw in. |
| 7 | **Install the CPU** | Central processing unit. | Open the socket latch, align the CPU (triangle marker), gently place, lock latch. |
| 8 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Keeps CPU from overheating. | Use a pea‑size amount of paste. Attach cooler per manufacturer instructions. |
| 9 | **Insert RAM** | Memory for multitasking. | Open DIMM slots, align notch, press until clicks. |
|10 | **Mount Storage (SSD/HDD)** | Data storage. | For M.2 SSDs, slide into M.2 slot and screw. For 2.5”/3.5” drives, use drive bays or brackets. |
|11 | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Handles rendering. | Remove PCIe slot covers, insert card, secure with screws. |
|12 | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components. | PSU 24‑pin to motherboard, 8‑pin CPU power, 6/8‑pin GPU power, SATA power for drives. |
|13 | **Connect Data Cables** | Data transfer. | SATA data cables to motherboard, NVMe uses M.2 slot. |
|14 | **Cable Management** | Keeps airflow and looks tidy. | Tuck cables behind the motherboard tray, use zip ties or Velcro straps. |
|15 | **Check Connections** | Avoid shorts or missing power. | Double‑check all screws, connectors, and that no metal is touching the case. |
|16 | **Close the Case** | Protect components. | Reattach side panels, screw in. |
|17 | **First Boot** | Verify hardware works. | Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse, power cable. Turn on. |
|18 | **Enter BIOS/UEFI** | Configure settings. | Set boot order, enable XMP for RAM, check temperatures. |
|19 | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Turn your PC into a usable machine. | Use a USB flash drive with Windows, Linux, or other OS installer. |
|20 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure hardware functions correctly. | Download latest drivers from component manufacturers. |
|21 | **Test & Benchmark** | Confirm stability and performance. | Run stress tests (Prime95, FurMark) and benchmarks (Cinebench, 3DMark). |
|22 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep your PC running smoothly. | Clean dust filters, update firmware, monitor temperatures. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- **CPU** – Intel i5/i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen 5/7/9
- **Motherboard** – ATX/MATX, matching socket
- **RAM** – 16 GB DDR4/DDR5 (or more for heavy workloads)
- **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070/3080 or AMD Radeon RX 6700/6800
- **Storage** – NVMe SSD (500 GB–2 TB) + optional HDD
- **PSU** – 650 W–850 W, 80+ Gold or better
- **Case** – ATX mid‑tower with good airflow
- **Cooling** – Stock cooler or aftermarket air/liquid cooler
- **Peripherals** – Monitor, keyboard, mouse, speakers/headset

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Shorted components** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; never touch metal contacts while inside the case. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow; install additional case fans if needed. |
| **Boot failure** | Check that all cables are firmly seated; verify BIOS settings. |
| **Driver conflicts** | Install drivers in the correct order: chipset → GPU → audio → network. |
| **Power issues** | Verify PSU wattage meets total draw; use a PSU calculator. |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & compatibility checker.  
- **YouTube Channels** – *Linus Tech Tips*, *JayzTwoCents*, *Paul’s Hardware* for visual guides.  
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community support.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, GPU, and PSU manuals.

---

### Final Thought

Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you full control over performance and aesthetics. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process. Happy building!
